blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: When can an attribution-derived anomaly justify changing a medical-imaging training set? We formulate attribution-driven curation as three separately testable claims: anomaly detection, harmfulness estimation, and intervention utility. We test the first and third using a patient-disjoint, identifier-preserving audit of a 3D convolutional classifier for computed tomography angiography aneurysm candidates. We identify 232 exactly zero-valued arrays among 1,201 positive patches, including 170 training positives, and invalidate a historical 321-patch attention-failure subgroup whose identifier-free records were joined to files by position. On the held-out test set, GradCAM++ spatial concentration is central for every candidate class, reversing the historical pattern. GradCAM++ and Integrated Gradients show negative rank-order agreement for positives, limiting method-independent anatomical interpretation. Across five paired training seeds, removing the 170 corrupted training positives yields AUC 0.9617 +/- 0.0044 versus 0.9652 +/- 0.0039 for full-data training (difference -0.0035; 95% CI -0.0082 to 0.0007). Excluding 34 raw-zero test positives widens rather than closes the gap, countering a blank-memorization explanation. Budget-matched random-removal controls suggest the result is not simply an effect of reducing training size. Input corruption does not necessarily imply that deletion improves generalization. Our framework makes leakage control, sample identity, and intervention testing explicit in attribution-driven medical-imaging data curation.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Attribution maps offer an attractive route from model interpretation to data
curation: score each image, inspect suspicious cases, and remove or repair
those judged anomalous. That workflow nevertheless combines distinct
inferences. A score can detect an unusual sample without showing that the
sample harms learning, and harmfulness does not guarantee that deletion is the
best intervention. Conflating these claims is consequential in clinical AI,
where a plausible heatmap may motivate changes to a limited or clinically
important training subset.

blocks.en:
Medical-imaging pipelines create particular audit risks. Multiple patches
can derive from one patient, so patch-wise splitting can contaminate
evaluation. Candidate generation, preprocessing, inference, attribution,
and clinical metadata are often executed separately and joined later;
losing sample identity at any interface can attach an explanation to the
wrong image ( Geirhos et al., 2020 ; Adebayo et al., 2018 ; Saporta et al., 2022 ) .

blocks.en:
We therefore ask: when does an attribution-derived anomaly justify a
training-data intervention? We decompose the question into three empirical
claims: anomaly detection (does the signal identify abnormal
samples?), harmfulness estimation (do those samples adversely affect
learning or generalization?), and intervention utility (does the
proposed deletion improve fixed held-out performance?). Success on one claim
does not establish the next. This paper tests anomaly detection and
intervention utility; harmfulness estimation remains an open link.

blocks.en:
Our case study is a two-stage intracranial aneurysm (IA) candidate pipeline
for computed tomography angiography (CTA), in which vesselness-derived
candidate locations are represented by 64 3 64^{3} patches and classified by a 3D
convolutional neural network (CNN). This study is an audit of a candidate
classifier, not an estimate of end-to-end diagnostic performance. The audit
tests whether historical attribution-based observations reproduce under
corrected methodology; it does not evaluate whether attribution maps are
faithful to model reasoning. The novelty lies in the audit construction and
empirical demonstration, not in the component methods individually.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Candidate-generation followed by patch classification is established for
intracranial aneurysm detection ( Frangi et al., 1998 ; Lauric et al., 2010 ; Nakao et al., 2018 ) . The two-stage design
introduces a hard interface between candidate extraction and learned
classification: every downstream evaluation inherits the identity and
quality of the extracted patch. Patient-disjoint splitting is necessary
whenever multiple patches derive from one patient, yet it is not
universally enforced in patch-level studies.

Confident Learning can flag likely label errors at scale ( Northcutt et al., 2021 ) , and data pruning can remove difficult or redundant
examples to improve training efficiency ( Paul et al., 2021 ) . However, an
accurate anomaly detector is not automatically an effective deletion
policy: removing a detected anomaly improves performance only if the
anomaly genuinely harms learning and the removal does not introduce a
worse bias.

blocks.en: 3 Audit Framework and Experimental Design
blocks.zh: 3 审计框架和实验设计

blocks.en: 3.1 Three separately testable claims
blocks.zh: 3.1 国家 三件可单独检验的索赔

blocks.en:
The audit follows a fixed sequence: an anomaly score is linked to raw
input by immutable patch identifier and checked against a direct quality
criterion; potential harmfulness is assessed without consulting test
labels; intervention utility is evaluated by retraining against both an
untouched full-data condition and a budget-matched random-removal condition.Patient separation and identifier integrity are enforced before model training, not verified after results are available.

使用不可移动的补丁标识符输入,并检查直接质量
标准;未经咨询测试评估潜在危害
标签;通过对两种标签进行再培训来评估干预效用。

blocks.en: 3.2 Clinical task and dataset
blocks.zh: 3.2 临床任务和数据集

blocks.en:
The frozen dataset derives from the RSNA 2025 Intracranial Aneurysm
Detection Challenge ( Radiological Society of North America, 2025 ) , a multi-institutional CTA collection
spanning four scanner manufacturers. It contains 7,742 CTA-derived patches
from 1,793 patient/scan groups: 1,201 positives and 6,541 negatives across three negative
subclasses—Frangi negatives (candidate locations triggered by the Frangi
vesselness filter ( Frangi et al., 1998 ) that are not true aneurysms), hard
negatives, and easy negatives. A seeded, stratified group split assigns patches to
training (1,256 patients), validation (270), and test (267) with zero
pairwise patient overlap. Complete counts appear in
Appendix A .

blocks.zh: 3.3 评价、模式和预处理

blocks.en:
All reported models use a 3D MONAI ResNet-10 ( 64 3 64^{3} input), trained from
scratch for 20 epochs with Adam ( LR = 10 − 4 \text{LR}=10^{-4} ), unweighted cross

the fixed test split is evaluated only after selection. A balanced training
subset contains 3,460 patches. Full specifications appear in
Appendix C . Preprocessing clips, smooths, and min–max
normalizes each patch; an identically zero raw array remains zero after
this transform, validating the raw-zero criterion.

blocks.zh: 3.4 归属和空间摘要

blocks.en:
GradCAM++ targets the positive-class logit at the last convolutional layer;
IG uses a zero baseline with 100 trapezoidal intervals. Both are computed for
every frozen patch (Appendix D ). We summarize spatial
concentration with the radial attribution ratio (RAR), the ratio of mean
outer-sphere to mean inner-sphere normalized attribution
(Appendix D ). RAR below one indicates central
concentration.

blocks.en: 3.6 Curation interventions and statistics
blocks.zh: 3.6 惩罚措施和统计

blocks.en:
The intervention study compares: (i) the full baseline with 868 training
positives; (ii) strict removal of all 170 raw-zero training positives; and
(iii) matched random removal of a fixed set of 170 randomly chosen training
positives (selection seed 42). All three conditions are trained with five
paired seeds (42–46) to separate the deletion effect from training-seed
variation. A complementary selection-variance control trains five distinct
random-removal subsets under a single training seed
(Appendix F , Table A9 ). All
other design choices are held constant.

blocks.en: 5 Discussion
blocks.zh: 5 讨论情况

blocks.en:
The strict rule has high construct validity: every flagged positive is an
identically zero array. Yet the intervention does not improve the full-data
point estimate across five paired training seeds, and the gap widens when
raw-zero test positives are excluded. The reusable boundary condition is
that anomaly is evidence for inspection, not sufficient evidence for
deletion . Notably, the zero-array anomaly was found by direct raw-input
inspection, not by the attribution workflow that was intended to detect such
issues; the heatmaps did not flag these patches.

blocks.en:
Interpretability validity also depends on identity provenance: immutable
sample identifiers are necessary because an attribution row without a
verifiable relationship to its image cannot sustain sample-level biological
claims. The corrected pipeline treats split membership and join coverage as
auditable artifacts, not implicit properties of file order.

blocks.en:
Notably, the defensible anomaly—232 zero-valued arrays—was identified
by direct raw-array inspection, not by the attribution scores themselves.
Attribution motivated the original investigation but did not produce the
quality signal; direct input QC did. This illustrates that attribution can
prioritize where to look without being the mechanism that confirms what is
wrong.
This study does not independently isolate harmfulness: the three-claim
framework is proposed, but only anomaly detection and intervention utility
are empirically evaluated. Whether zero-valued patches actively degrade
learned representations—rather than merely contributing uninformative
gradients—would require influence-function or leave-one-out analyses
beyond the scope of this retrospective audit. Because only positive patches are removed, both strict and random
conditions reduce the effective positive prior under unweighted
cross-entropy. This confound is shared between strict and random arms
(and cancels in their comparison) but is not controlled in the
strict-versus-baseline contrast.

patient through transformed model input. A credible audit should preserve
these links. The three-claim decomposition clarifies action: direct raw QC

blocks.en: 6 Limitations
blocks.zh: 6. 限制

blocks.en:
This retrospective audit covers one inherited dataset, one disease, one
preprocessing path, and one model family (MONAI ResNet-10); architecture
dependence remains untested. Source CTA volumes are unavailable, so the
upstream cause of zero patches cannot be reconstructed. The RAR reversal
(Section 4 ) cannot be isolated to the corrected
patient-disjoint split versus the retrained model, because the historical
model checkpoint is not recoverable. Five paired training seeds quantify
seed variation for the deletion comparison; the test-patient bootstrap
captures test-sample uncertainty. The harmfulness link in the three-claim
framework is not directly tested. Training used no augmentation, limiting
generalization claims. Attribution faithfulness was not established with
causal perturbation tests. Lesion-size values are inherited rather than new
blinded measurements. We use patient-cluster analyses where IDs support
them; remaining analyses are descriptive. This patch-classification audit
does not measure end-to-end candidate recall.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
A patient-disjoint, identifier-preserving audit rejected two historical
mechanistic interpretations, isolated a real zero-input anomaly, and found no
held-out benefit from its targeted deletion. The result is that each link
from explanation to action requires separate evidence: attribution-driven
curation should separately establish anomaly, harmfulness, and intervention
utility.
